newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds take beating from Ifo, M3 but stay resilient.
newsitem.headline: Bunds take beating from Ifo, M3 but stay resilient.

text.p: German Bunds took a beating on Wednesday after news of strong M3 data and business confidence in October. But dealers said they did not expect a big sell-off and that Bunds may test their highs again by end-1996.
December Bund futures fell as low as 100.69, down 59 basis points from the contract high of 101.28 reached earlier, but later recovered amid short-covering to 100.90.
The yield on the benchmark 10-year April 2006 Bund rose to 5.83 percent by 1540 GMT from 5.78 percent in early trade.
Dealers said Bunds could fall to around 100.50 or lower in coming days but saw strong demand between 100.20 and 100.30.

The drop accelerated after Bund futures fell though key support at 100.85, triggering stop-loss orders. But a second technical support level around the day's low of 100.69 held, causing short-covering, dealers said.

The data dampened what little hope remained of another slight cut in German interest rates and had thereby hit shorter-dated maturities more than the long end of the market which was likely to consolidate, dealers and analysts said.
The long end of the market remained supported by the steepness of the German yield curve, with investors still attracted by high returns from longer-dated maturities.
But with rate hopes fading fast and yields at the short end of the market edging higher the yield curve was set to flatten in the the short-term, dealers said.
Bunds also remained underpinned by favourable conditions in the U.S. market, where Treasuries remained buoyed by fresh economic data suggesting the economy was slowing with no signs of inflation.
The Bund/T-note spread was steady around 44 basis points.
